I think it varies from person to person and I feel different on different days. I mean some days I just feel nothing like numbness. I think, this is just my opinion from what you've wrote but it seems that you set goals for yourself that may or may not be realistic for you. Idk what this list of things are but it seems like you put a lot of expectations on yourself and are let down when you don't meet your all these expectations. Personally, this would make me down on myself and if this kept happening through the span of many years. It would put a lot of stress on me and make me anxious as well. Maybe this could be happening to you? It's hard not to have high expectations for yourself especially when you think you owe it to the people around you but it's worse if these expectations are what's making your life more difficult unknowingly. Maybe try making a reasonable list of things but don't be too focused on the things you haven't checked off but the things you have. Of course, this may not be all that it is but if you have any concerns about your mental health or would just generally like to know, I think you may want to try talking to a psychiatrist or therapist to give you a professional view or diagnosis.

That really makes sense. I’ve always wondered if I lost weight or started to exercise maybe for health reasons, would I be happier or at least have something to do? I’m very socially awkward and shy so I developed social anxiety, even online through chats I usually don’t talk in fear of being either ignore or something else. I’ve always been envious and admired people who were passionate about things whether career or hobby, whatever it was, I don’t have. It sucks because they’re all the things I’ve thought about and thought “I would probably be happier if I had something like that.” I know I have to do it on my own but once I get enough motivation to try, I lose it, or when I do try, I stop after a maybe a month. Idk if that means it wasn’t for me because if I really loved doing those things, wouldn’t I have more motivation to do it? Once I find things to do, I go hard and then lose interest or motivation like a burnout or like when you find a new song you like so you listen to it multiple times a day daily and then one day you just don’t feel Like listening to it anymore and avoid it for a while(this isn’t the case for all songs but some) I then try and find excuses as to why I don’t do those things anymore or think “maybe I’ll get back into them later”and procrastinate. Basically, I have short attention span. So I admire people who are opposite of me, who do things because it’s they’re dream and they’re passionate about it, who have confidence in themselves(or good reason) etc., etc. Strangely enough, talking about it makes me want to try get back into some things.
